title: XOR-related-key security of five-round affine KAFw
summary: Determine whether every five-round key-alternating Feistel cipher with whitening is XOR-related-key secure under the source affine key-schedule condition.

formal_statement.body: Let a five-round key-alternating Feistel cipher with whitening (KAFw) use the affine whitening and round-key maps defined in the source. In the source XOR-induced related-key strong-PRP experiment, is the construction secure for every such schedule satisfying $M_1\Delta \ne M_5\Delta$ for every nonzero $\Delta$ (equivalently, $\ker(M_1-M_5)=\{0\}$)? A compatible attack would refute the conjecture.

scope.domain: Five-round key-alternating Feistel ciphers with whitening in the ideal-function or ideal-permutation model
assumptions: The KAFw construction and XOR-induced related-key strong-PRP experiment are those defined by the source
Whitening-key and round-key transformations are affine over the n-bit XOR vector space
For every nonzero key difference Delta, M1 Delta is not equal to M5 Delta
The adversary has the source encryption/decryption and ideal-round-primitive interfaces
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether the source XOR-related-key strong-PRP security claim holds for every five-round KAFw schedule satisfying ker(M1-M5)={0}; a proof or a compatible attack for the complete stated family is still absent.

citations.label: Chun Guo, Understanding the Related-Key Security of Feistel Ciphers From a Provable Perspective

progress.summary: The source conjectures security in the five-round collision-free case and explicitly leaves its proof for future work.
citation_labels: Chun Guo, Understanding the Related-Key Security of Feistel Ciphers From a Provable Perspective
